n: Basilica of Saint Mary of the Chorus
w: Completed in 1774, this Baroque parish church anchors the Parte Vieja, San Sebastian's old town between Mount Urgull and the harbour. It carries the Basque name Andre Mariaren basilika and the Spanish Nuestra Senora del Coro, and has since been raised to minor basilica, a title Rome reserves for churches of note.
s: Baroque basilica at the heart of the old fishing town
_facts: Completed 1774 in Baroque style
Located in the Parte Vieja (Old Town)
Raised to minor basilica status
Also known as Nuestra Senora del Coro

n: Good Shepherd Cathedral of San Sebastián
w: Built in the last years of the 19th century in a strongly vertical Neo-Gothic style, this is the largest church in Gipuzkoa. It serves the Diocese of San Sebastian but has held cathedral rank only since 1953. Dedicated to the Good Shepherd, its spire dominates the skyline above La Concha bay.
s: Neo-Gothic cathedral, tallest church in Gipuzkoa
_facts: Built in Neo-Gothic style in the late 19th century
Largest church in Gipuzkoa
Cathedral status only since 1953
Seat of the Diocese of San Sebastian

w: This 123-metre hill has guarded La Concha bay since the 12th century, later reinforced as borders hardened in the 1500s. Mota Castle crowns the summit with old barracks and a chapel, plus a 12-metre statue of Christ added in 1950. It saw action in the 1813 Siege before the city bought it in 1924.
s: Fortified hill guarding the bay since the 12th century
_facts: Fortified as a defensive point from the 12th century
Mota Castle sits at the summit with barracks, warehouse, chapel
Saw action in the 1813 Siege of San Sebastian and the Carlist Wars
Sold to the city council in 1924; summit now houses a history museum

w: Housed in a former Dominican monastery at the foot of Mount Urgull, San Telmo Museoa has occupied its Zuloaga plaza site since 1932. A 2011 renovation added a modern extension to the convent and reframed the collection around Basque society, arts and history, earning a mention in the 2013 best European museum contest.
s: Basque history museum inside a former monastery
_facts: Former Dominican monastery, occupied since 1932
2011 extension added to the convent
Focuses on Basque culture, arts and history
Special mention, 2013 European Museum of the Year contest

w: Two carriages haul passengers 320 metres up a steep cliff on a single track with a mid-point passing loop, linking Ondarreta Beach to the Monte Igeldo Amusement Park above. Listed as a piece of industrial heritage, the short climb frames some of the best coastal views around, over La Concha bay.
s: Cliffside funicular linking the beach to Monte Igeldo
_facts: Runs 320 metres up a cliff on a single track with a passing loop
Connects Ondarreta Beach to Monte Igeldo Amusement Park
Listed as an industrial heritage site
Offers coastal views over La Concha Bay

w: Designed by architect Jose de Goikoa and inaugurated in 1878, this cemetery took its first burial on 12 August that year. Its pantheons -- family tombs built as small classical monuments -- were the work of various artists, giving the grounds more the air of an open-air sculpture gallery than a municipal graveyard.
_facts: Designed by architect Jose de Goikoa
Inaugurated 1878; first burial 12 August 1878
Pantheons built in classical style by various artists

w: For most of the 20th century, municipal nurseries here grew plants for San Sebastian's public gardens, until the city moved out in 2008 and shut the site. Neighbours reopened it in 2015 and have run it since, fighting off a 2016 plan to clear it for housing. Two 19th-century water tanks survive on the grounds.
s: Reclaimed nursery park with two 19th-century water tanks
_facts: Supplied plants for San Sebastian's public gardens until 2008
Closed 2008; reopened by local residents in 2015
Residents blocked a 2016 council plan to build housing on the site
Two 19th-century water tanks remain on site

w: Designed by engineer Erich Heidrich and opened in 1928 at Monte Igeldo Amusement Park, this is the oldest steel roller coaster still operating anywhere in the world. Built as a scenic railway with wooden cars on steel bogies, its track runs partly along the top of a coastal wall, with a brakeman riding each train.
s: 1928 scenic railway, the oldest steel coaster running
_facts: Opened 1928, designed by Erich Heidrich
Oldest operating steel roller coaster in the world
Track runs in a trough, partly along a coastal wall
A brakeman rides each train to control its speed
